extracted.intended_audience: agency staff, regulators, legal scholars, and public commenters interested in notice-and-comment rulemaking and the impact of generative AI on public commenting
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative standards for producing and for agencies assessing public comments filed in administrative rulemaking, with special attention to effects of generative AI and mass-comment campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include specific personal details that AI can't fabricate
rubrics_metrics.description: A truly effective comment that won't be confused with AI-mass-generated content should include specific personal details that AI can't fabricate (specific dates, places, names of relevant officials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete, verifiable facts about the commenter’s experience (e.g., exact dates of events, locations, named officials) so the comment is demonstrably tied to a real person and situation rather than appearing generically produced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference the commenter's unique factual circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference the unique factual circumstances of the commenter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the regulation would affect the commenter’s actual, particular circumstances (employment, local conditions, precise business operations) rather than making abstract or general claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite documents personally reviewed by the commenter
rubrics_metrics.description: Cite documents the commenter has personally reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include references to specific documents, reports, or records the commenter has read and can discuss in detail, which signals first-hand engagement and substantiates assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tie arguments to specific data the commenter has access to
rubrics_metrics.description: Make arguments tied to specific data the commenter has access to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use and cite particular datasets, measurements, or business records available to the commenter to ground claims in verifiable evidence rather than sweeping statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with agency-specific questions to show genuine understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage with the agency's specific questions in ways that show genuine understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond directly to the issues and question prompts in the rulemaking docket, demonstrating familiarity with the agency’s framing and the technical/regulatory details under consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive versus low-information comment distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate substantive comments from low-information or form-letter comments—though that distinction becomes harder in a post-LLM era.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should consider indicators of substantive content (personalized facts, data, document engagement, tailored legal/regulatory analysis) and beware that stylistic variation produced by AI can mask low-information submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying solely on surface-level personalization
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not rely only on superficial personalization (small rhetorical tweaks) which can make form letters look individualized without adding substantive content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True personalization should be tied to verifiable personal facts and specific impacts rather than mere changes in wording or tone; otherwise comments remain low-information despite surface differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection — improve duplicate-detection algorithms
rubrics_metrics.description: Existing deduplication tools may become less effective; agencies are likely to develop better duplicate-detection algorithms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in more sophisticated methods that go beyond exact-match detection to identify coordinated mass campaigns that use varied phrasing produced by generative models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detection — cluster/comments by semantic similarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Cluster comments by semantic similarity (not just exact match) as a detection approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use semantic clustering or other NLP techniques to group comments that express the same underlying claims or arguments even when surface wording differs, to identify mass-coordinated inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identity verification measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Implement identity verification (CAPTCHA, email confirmation) to limit automated or bot-driven submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical authentication steps (e.g., CAPTCHAs, email or account confirmation) can raise the cost of mass automated submission and help ensure commenters are real individuals, though they do not prove substantive authenticity on their own.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference commenter identity with claimed credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-reference commenter identity with claimed credentials to validate expertise or standing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where commenters assert professional or organizational qualifications, agencies may check those claims against available records or registries to assess credibility and the weight to give the comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require or consider disclosure of AI assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: Question whether and what disclosure should be required when AI generates substantial portions of a comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may consider rules or guidance asking commenters to disclose use of generative AI when it materially contributed to content, to help evaluate provenance and intent—though the paper frames this as an open policy question rather than settled guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decide policy on treatment parity for AI-assisted comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether agencies should treat AI-assisted comments the same as fully human comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must decide if AI-assisted comments will be accepted, weighted, or handled differently; this is an unresolved question bearing on procedural fairness and administrative burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate increased agency resource needs for comment analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources dedicated to comment analysis must increase as AI makes detection and substantive assessment harder.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan for greater staffing, technical tools, or processes to review comments, adjudicate mass campaigns, and respond appropriately to substantively varied but potentially coordinated inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize that agency response burden will increase
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency response burden increases proportionally with more and harder-to-assess comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect more time and effort will be required to determine which comments merit formal responses, to parse substantive input from noise, and to document decision-making in the administrative record.
